newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Belgian shares hold breath as Dow stumbles.
newsitem.headline: Belgian shares hold breath as Dow stumbles.

text.p: Belgian share prices were stripped of nearly one percent on Friday, but dealers said next week's performance would depend entirely on the Dow's resilience.
"Everything hinges on New York," Gert De Mesure at Delen Bank said. The Dow was about 50 points lower in early trade.
The Bel-20 ended near the day's low when a technical reaction after this week's record run was exacerbated by weakness on Wall Street and in bonds.
It closed down 0.96 percent, or 21.27 points, at 2,202.22 with a modest two billion francs worth of Belgian shares traded.

De Mesure said that with the dollar still relatively strong and interest rates still relatively low, the Bel-20 would probably consolidate at current levels in the short run barring a surprise on Wall Street.
He expected it to slip later in the year as the dollar was bound to weaken and rates due to rise.
He said the index was also due to be stripped of some 40 to 50 points during upcoming the dividend payment season.
He said the day's main losers were those who had gained most earlier in the week, including non-ferrous metals firm Union Miniere which dropped 2.5 percent to 2,910 francs.
Other shares falling victim to profit-taking were insurer Fortis AG, which lost 2.0 percent to 3,080 francs, and holding company Societe Generale de Belgique, which closed 2.2 percent lower at 3,080.

Retailer Colruyt and Kredietbank (KB) were the only two Bel-20 gainers. Colruyt, already in vogue in recent days on newspaper reports it had increased its market share in Belgium, added 0.3 percent to 14,650 francs. Dealers continued to prefer Colruyt over fellow retailers GIB and Delhaize. KB continued to benefit from 'buy' recommendations from rivals Generale Bank and CERA.
Bank Dexia CC continued to slide on surprise news earlier this week of a new share issue by its controlling shareholder and as a result of arbitrage against shares in French partner bank Dexia CLF.
Dexia CC, which fell four percent on Thursday, lost another two percent at 3,410 francs.
